name: King's Indian Defence
summary: 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 3.Nc3 Bg7 4.e4 d6: Black lets White build a big centre, then strikes at it with ...e5 or ...c5. When the centre closes, the game becomes a race: White on the queenside, Black with ...f5 and ...f4 against the king.

black: Fianchetto, castle, then strike the centre with ...e5 (or ...c5).
When White closes the centre with d5, attack where your pawns point: ...Nd7 or ...Ne8, then ...f5, ...f4 and ...g5.
Do not let e4 tempt you: the c3 knight guards it, and ...Nxe4 tricks usually fail.
When the centre opens with ...exd4, aim ...Re8 and the g7 bishop at e4.
white: Use the space: c4 and c5 and a queenside pawn advance when the centre is closed.
Keep e4 safe with f3 when Black's pieces pile up on it.
In the Sämisch, play Be3 and Qd2, and sometimes castle long and attack with g4 and h4.

structures.name: Closed centre: d5 and e4 against d6 and e5
structures.text: The pawn chains point to the wings. White attacks on the queenside with c5; Black attacks on the kingside with ...f5, ...f4 and ...g5. Whoever arrives first usually wins.

structures.name: Open centre after ...exd4
structures.text: Black gives up the e5 point for piece play: ...Re8 and the g7 bishop hit e4, and ...Nc6 or ...Nbd7 add pressure. White's centre becomes a target.

black: g7 bishop: blocked by e5 in the closed lines, but it comes alive when the kingside or the centre opens.
f6 knight: retreats to d7 or e8 so the f-pawn can advance.
e7 knight: goes to g6 to support ...f4 and the attack.
f8 rook: f7 or f6 to join the attack on the f-file.
white: c3 knight: guards e4 and d5.
e2 bishop: quiet, but it defends the king when Black attacks.
Queenside pawns: b4 and c5 to open the c-file.
f3 pawn: guards e4 and stops ...Ng4.

lines.name: Classical, 9.Ne1: the race begins
lines.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Nf3 O-O 6. Be2 e5 7. O-O Nc6 8. d5 Ne7 9. Ne1 Nd7 10. Nd3 f5 11. Bd2 Nf6 12. f3 f4

notes.1...Nf6: Controls e4 and keeps the choice of set-up open.
notes.5...O-O: King safety first; the strike comes next.
notes.6...e5: The King's Indian break: Black claims a share of the centre.
notes.8.d5: White closes the centre and gains space.
notes.8...Ne7: The knight goes towards the kingside, where Black will attack.
notes.9.Ne1: The knight heads for d3 to support c5.

lines.name: Sämisch, 5.f3: ...e5 and ...c6
lines.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. f3 O-O 6. Be3 e5 7. Nge2 c6 8. Qd2 Nbd7 9. d5 cxd5 10. cxd5 a6

notes.5.f3: The Sämisch: e4 is rock solid and ...Ng4 is ruled out.
notes.9...cxd5: Opens the c-file before White can castle long in peace.
notes.10...a6: Prepares ...b5 to gain space on the queenside.

lines.name: Fianchetto Variation: ...e5 against g3
lines.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nf3 Bg7 4. g3 O-O 5. Bg2 d6 6. O-O Nbd7 7. Nc3 e5 8. e4 c6 9. h3 Qb6

notes.4.g3: White mirrors: a quiet set-up with the bishop on g2.

lines.name: Averbakh, 6.Bg5: hit back with ...c5
lines.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Be2 O-O 6. Bg5 c5 7. d5 e6 8. Qd2 exd5 9. exd5 Re8 10. Nf3 Bf5

notes.6.Bg5: Pins the knight and makes ...e5 harder.
notes.6...c5: Hits d4 instead: the bishop on g5 has left the queenside.
notes.9...Re8: The rook takes the open file.
notes.10...Bf5: Develops actively; Black's pieces are free.

lines.name: Exchange Variation: no fear of the queen trade
lines.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Nf3 O-O 6. Be2 e5 7. dxe5 dxe5 8. Qxd8 Rxd8 9. Bg5 Re8 10. Nd5 Nxd5 11. cxd5 c6 12. Bc4 cxd5 13. Bxd5 Nd7

notes.7.dxe5: White trades queens, hoping for a dull endgame.
notes.8...Rxd8: The rook takes back; Black's king is already safe.
notes.9.Bg5: Pins the f6 knight against the d8 rook.
notes.13...Nd7: Heads for c5 or f6; the endgame is level.

traps.name: 9...Nxe4?: e4 is not loose
traps.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Nf3 O-O 6. Be2 e5 7. O-O Nc6 8. d5 Ne7 9. Ne1 Nxe4 10. Nxe4 f5 11. Nc3

notes.9.Ne1: The f3 knight leaves, and e4 looks short of defenders.
notes.9...Nxe4: The mistake: Black hopes ...f5 will win the piece back.

traps.punishment: 10.Nxe4 f5 11.Nc3: the knight simply retreats and nothing is forked. Black is a piece for a pawn down. The c3 knight guards e4; play 9...Nd7 or 9...Ne8 and attack with ...f5 instead.

traps.name: 9.Qc2?: the e4 pawn needs f3
traps.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Nf3 O-O 6. Be2 e5 7. O-O exd4 8. Nxd4 Re8 9. Qc2 Nxe4 10. Nxe4 Bxd4

notes.7...exd4: Black opens the centre to aim at e4.
notes.8...Re8: The rook and the f6 knight now hit e4.
notes.9.Qc2: The mistake: the queen leaves d1, and the d4 knight loses its guard.

traps.punishment: 9...Nxe4 10.Nxe4 Bxd4: Black wins a clean pawn, and the e4 knight is pinned against the e2 bishop. White had to play 9.f3, guarding e4 with a pawn.
